jobs.description:
About the role

As Process Engineer Lithography, you will be responsible for ensuring stable, capable, and reproducible lithography processes in a high-volume semiconductor manufacturing environment. You will drive process improvements, solve complex technical challenges, support the introduction of new technologies, and work closely with production, maintenance, quality, and development teams to achieve excellence in safety, quality, productivity, and cost performance.

This is your new role

- Ensure stable, capable, and reproducible lithography processes in daily semiconductor manufacturing operations
- Monitor and improve process performance using SPC, process capability indicators, and manufacturing data analysis
- Investigate process deviations, non-conforming lots, and yield excursions and drive sustainable corrective actions
- Identify process-related quality issues and support continuous yield and defect reduction initiatives
- Support root-cause analysis activities using structured problem-solving methodologies such as 5Why and 8D
- Define, execute, analyze, and document experiments to improve process capability, productivity, quality, and cost performance
- Support qualification, release, and implementation of new processes, materials, and equipment
- Contribute to process change management, industrialization projects, and technology transfers into production
- Create and maintain process documentation, work instructions, OCAPs, specifications, and training materials
- Conduct technical training and knowledge sharing for production teams
- Participate in FMEA activities and support risk assessment and mitigation measures

This is you

- University degree in Physics, Chemistry, Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Microsystems Engineering, or a comparable technical discipline
- First professional experience in semiconductor manufacturing, process engineering, or a comparable high-tech production environment is advantageous
- Knowledge of lithography processes and semiconductor manufacturing technologies is desirable
- Strong analytical thinking skills combined with a structured and systematic working approach
- Passion for solving technical problems and driving continuous improvement
- Ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities in a dynamic manufacturing environment
- Strong communication and teamwork skills
- High level of ownership, initiative, and accountability
- Practical mindset combined with attention to detail and quality orientation
- Good German and English communication skills, both written and spoken

TU Darmstadt stands for excellent and relevant science. We are playing a decisive role in shaping far-reaching processes of global change-from energy transition to artificial intelligence-through outstanding scientific knowledge and innovative academic programmes. We group our cutting-edge research into three fields: Energy and Environment, Information and Intelligence, Matter and Materials. We are a university with strong ties to the Frankfurt Rhine-Main metropolitan region and a very strong international focus. We are committed to European values and European integration.

The Centre for Synthetic Biology at TU Darmstadt is a university-wide interdisciplinary research initiative bringing together biologists and biochemists with computational scientists and machine learning researchers. The PhD candidate will conduct research in AI method development for the design of novel RNA molecules with application in advanced therapeutic modalities.
Work on an interdisciplinary topic at the intersection of machine learning / AI and synthetic biology
Learn the mathematics and algorithms of state-of-the-art RNA language models
Learn the mathematics and algorithms of state-of-the-art diffusion models for generation of new RNA and protein molecules
Advance AI methods and models for the design of novel RNA molecules that get conditionally activated upon binding of specific diagnostic RNA molecules
Find novel ways to Incorporate structure and sequence information in RNA AI-models.
Build novel AI models for quantitative functional prediction of RNA designs
Work in close collaboration with experimentalists that conduct high-throughput assays for the characterization of these novel RNA molecules

An excellent university science degree (Master’s/Diploma) in computer science, electrical engineering, physics or mathematics. Master’s/Diploma degree must be completed prior to the start of employment.
Very good programming skills in python; finished larger scientific software projects
Advanced academic training / background in machine learning and AI methods.
Experience with dedicated AI methods for molecular design is a big plus.
Solid understanding of molecular biology and cell biology is a big plus.
Willingness and drive to work on an interdisciplinary project beyond traditional boundaries.

In addition, you bring:

Fluency in English for communication in an international team and for writing scientific publications

On a personal level, you distinguish yourself through:

Analytical thinking and a high degree of self-organization
Curiosity and creativity
Openness to working in an interdisciplinary and international team

Your application should include:

a cover letter explaining succinctly why you want to join this project
your CV
bachelor’s and master’s degree certificates and transcript of records
a list of publications / talks / poster contributions
contact details of 2 referees
Technical University of Darmstadt offers varied and challenging assignments, freedom to work independently, the latest technologies, good collaboration between colleagues in partnership, needs-based training opportunities and customised personnel development.

Institute of Physiology and Cell Biology. Starting date: as soon as possible, at the latest September 1,2026.

Area of responsibility

The Institute of Physiology and Cell Biology aims to recruit a highly motivated post-doctoral scientistto join the Cell Biology group, headed by Prof. Dr. Sjoerd van Wijk. We study how ubiquitination andautophagy control cell survival, programmed cell death, inflammation and cell differentiation inbroad pathophysiological settings, including oncology and infection. For this, human and animalpre-clinical experimental systems, including cell lines, primary cells, organoids and iPSC-derivedcells, will be integrated with cell biology with biochemistry, molecular biology and omicsapproaches, including CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, super-resolution and confocal microscopy andmass-spectrometry. For examples of recent research, see Wächtershäuser et al, Signal TransductTarget Ther, 11(1):204; Zein et al, Autophagy, 21(5):1075-1095 and Weinelt et al, Cell Death Dis,15(1):77.

The position will be closely involved in shaping the research group, setting up the lab and planningand performing independent research at the interface of cell biology, biochemistry and molecularbiology with imaging and computational data analysis. The successful candidate will play centralroles in collaborations between different scientific and clinical research groups and in developinginnovative approaches in comparative cell biology to improve animal and human health. Theposition furthermore combines opportunities for teaching, scientific and academic qualification(Habilitation) and the development of independent research projects within the scope of the group.

Key Focus Areas:

• Independent experimental scientific research in comparative cell biology.

• Teaching and supervision of Bachelor, Master and PhD students/Habilitation.

• Coordination of lab setup and daily running.

• Contribution to the development and implementation of integrative analytical approaches forcell biology, biochemistry and molecular biology, incl. multi-omics, CRISPR/Cas-basedapproaches, imaging and bioinformatic image analysis.

• Support in the analysis of large datasets (e.g., RNA-seq, single-cell data and imaging).

• Support in the preparation of scientific publications and grant applications, for example for theGerman Research Foundation.

• Organization of scientific exchange activities, workshops and project meetings.

Recruitment requirements:

• A university degree and doctoral degree/PhD in (Molecular) Cell Biology, Biochemistry, MolecularBiology, Biology, Veterinary Medicine ("Approbation"), or a related discipline.

• Excellent written and spoken German and English language skills.

• Experience with, or strong interest in, multiscale imaging, CRISPR/Cas-based methods andprimary cell/tissue culture (organoids).

• Basic knowledge in the analysis of high-dimensional biological datasets, particularly microscopicdatasets.

• Knowledge of additional disciplines, including systems biology, gene regulation, epigenomics ormultiscale data integration, is advantageous.

Required professional knowledge and personal skills:

• Ability to communicate complex scientific concepts across disciplinary boundaries.

• Independent, structured and solution-oriented working style.

• Excellent organizational, communication and teamwork skills.

• Willingness to contribute to scientific coordination, develop independent research questions andparticipate in the preparation of publications and grant applications.

• Curious, strong analytical and conceptual thinking skills combined with the ability to developinnovative solutions.

• Flexibility and willingness to rapidly familiarize oneself with new technologies and researchareas.

What we offer:

The employment relationship is subject to the public sector collective agreement on the federalstates (TV-L). Severely disabled applicants will be given priority in the case of equal suitability. Therefore, it strives to increase the underrepresented gender in the respective area.
